reason: Both pick Postgres with SKIP LOCKED and stress transactional enqueue and using an existing library. A's SQS limits (15-min delay, 12-hr visibility) are accurate, and it adds a PgBouncer caveat, an idempotency note, separate queues, and a concrete revisit trigger. B has factual slips about SQS: it says SQS lacks native delay (it has up to 15 minutes) and gives an outdated 256KB payload limit (now 1 MiB). B's advice not to hold a transaction open during job execution and its report isolation tip are good, but it gives no migration trigger for Postgres. A is more accurate and more complete.
